**Why they must be OFF, not standby:** A reflow oven in standby still draws 36% of its 70 kW rating — about 25.2 kW per oven — for as long as it stays on, producing nothing. [source: docs/knowledge/sop/SOP-02_weekend_shutdown.md#SOP-02 Weekend Shutdown > Why reflow ovens must be OFF, not standby]

Note: the off-schedule rule would flag this, but only after 120 minutes above 20% of rating, so the real benefit is preventing it before the weekend. [source: docs/knowledge/sop/SOP-02_weekend_shutdown.md#SOP-02 Weekend Shutdown > Why reflow ovens must be OFF, not standby]

answer:
Per SOP-03 / EM-02:

**Shed first:** EV charging (EV-01) — paused first because it removes its full load with no effect on production. [source: docs/knowledge/energy-management/EM-02_demand_management.md#EM-02 Demand Management > Load-shed playbook]

**Never shed:** the server room (DC-01), running molders mid-cycle (IM-01–IM-04), and reflow ovens with boards inside (RF-01–RF-03). [source: docs/knowledge/energy-management/EM-02_demand_management.md#EM-02 Demand Management > Load-shed playbook > Never shed]

The full shed order is: (1) pause EV charging, (2) delay the next burn-in loading (BI-01, BI-02), (3) raise chilled-water setpoint +1°C (CH-01, CH-02), (4) lower compressed-air pressure 0.5 bar (AC-01–AC-03). Restore in reverse order once demand is below the 1,125 kW warning line. [source: docs/knowledge/energy-management/EM-02_demand_management.md#EM-02 Demand Management > Load-shed playbook]
